card.summary: Free upload and share, 'FREE & always will be', with 'Unlimited files upload ... no limitation in size or speed'; storage and download volume limits are only...

free_tier.stated: Free upload and share, 'FREE & always will be', with 'Unlimited files upload ... no limitation in size or speed'; storage and download volume limits are only stated for premium.
free_tier.notes: The free column is advertised as unlimited upload; the premium plan is what buys 'Unlimited storage' and 'Unlimited download... with no speed restrictions'.

per_object_cap.stated: 'Upload your files with different methods and no limitation in size or speed.'

retention.stated: not stated on the pages read

egress.terms: Premium: 'Unlimited download ... with no speed restrictions' plus '500 GB traffic/daily'. The daily figure is the real ceiling; 'unlimited' is the marketing word above it.
egress.free_allowance: none stated for the free tier; premium carries 500 GB/day

record.interface_detail: Web upload with 'different methods'; no API, FTP or remote-upload endpoint is published on the pages read.
record.tooling: Browser only as read. The host is on the Leechall and PrimeLeech generator lists, so a leecher is the only scripted path found.
record.chaining: 500 GB/day is fifteen times the 34.1 GB/day 1 TiB of monthly transfer needs, so transfer is not the constraint here. The constraint is that nothing on the page prices storage separately, which makes it a transfer pipe rather than an archive.

limits.value: 500 GB of traffic per day on premium

record.limits_note: The payment-rules block adds surcharges: '10% credit card fees are added to card payments', '20% paypal fees are added to paypal payments in USD'. The effective PayPal price of the 30-day plan is therefore about €17.99, not €14.99.
record.binding_note: 500 GB/day is far above what 1 TiB a month needs, so nothing in the vocabulary actually fails at that scale, but volume-quota is the only metered quantity the vendor states and it is the field a larger client would hit. Treated as the binding kind rather than none because the 20% PayPal surcharge is a price wall, not a byte wall.

identity_cost.detail: Checkout by card or PayPal, with fees added on top. The page warns 'dont use VPN server for payments', which is an egress restriction at the payment step rather than at download.

record.reliability_note: A payment attempted from a VPN is a stated way to fail the order; the fee surcharge is applied at checkout rather than shown in the advertised price.
record.confidence_note: Plan prices, the 500 GB/day figure and the fee block are read from the vendor's premium page. The free tier's real storage cap is not printed anywhere read, so 'unlimited' here is the vendor's word and not a measurement.

evidence.proved: the four prices (30 days €14.99, 90 days €32.99, 180 days €55.99, 365 days €89.99), each with 'Unlimited storage' and '500 GB traffic/daily', plus the 10%/20% card and PayPal surcharges
'It's FREE & always will be', 1,000,000+ files, and the free upload claim with 'no limitation in size or speed'

record.price_per_tb_month: EUR 14.99 per 30 days for 500 GB/day traffic
record.notes: The 365-day plan at €89.99 is €7.40 a month. The 10 GB top-up at €5.00 is the only pay-per-volume item on the page.
